questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Penelope's web

options.label: A
options.text: To be able to punch very powerfully

options.label: C
options.text: Defuse an angry or tense situation by frank discussion

options.label: D
options.text: Suppress, or destroy something at an early stage

questions.solution: The idiom 'Penelope's web' means 'An endless job'. Hence, option b) is the correct answer. 'Nip something in the bud' means 'Suppress or destroy something at an early stage'. 'Clear the air' means 'Defuse an angry or tense situation by frank discussion'. 'Pack a wallop' means 'To be able to punch very powerfully'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'disguise' from the passage.
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Sunrise Foods, just a few blocks from my house, is marked by a glossy freestanding sign, a cheery egg-yolk yellow against an often grey, wintering Toronto sky. Back in December, just before I turned 14, Tracey recruited a bunch of us from the school lunch table to work here in her uncle's new bagel and smoked fish store. Now, six months on, all my peers are gone. But I have learned to tell whitefish chubs with their oily, golden hue from goldeye that wrinkles away from the skin. I've learned how to sheath my arm in a plastic bag and plunge it into a barrel of gutted herring, floating in their vegetable oil pond. How to act like I wasn't afraid to touch the fish until I wasn't afraid to touch the fish.

At the barrel I re-tie my white apron over the green Roots Athletics T-shirt I bought with my first paycheck, protecting it from oil splashes that never wash out. My dirty-blonde waves are pinned on top of my head with a clip of faux pearls. A berry-scented hair spray from a purple bottle helps disguise the fish smell. I'd had an argument with my mother just before I was hired at Sunrise. She was annoyed that the sleeves of my winter coat no longer reached my wrists, that I was yanking my shirt sleeves down to my mittens to cover the gap. My growing body and its expense had slipped her mind. I had to agree to chip in my birthday money, but I got to choose the store and the new coat. Then it hit me: birthday cards only come once a year. I really needed a job.
questions.solution:
The second paragraph states that "A berry-scented hair spray from a purple bottle helps disguise the fish smell." In the given sentence, the word 'disguise' means '(of a taste, smell, etc.) prevent the perception of (another sensation).' Therefore, 'mask' which means '(of a taste, smell, etc.) prevent the perception of (another sensation)' is the correct synonym of the given word.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Facade: the principal front of a building, that faces onto a street or open space.

Mislead: cause (someone) to have a wrong idea or impression.

Blanket: cover completely with a thick layer of something.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Subject to sudden and unpredictable changes of mood or mind
questions.solution:
Astute - having or showing an ability to accurately assess situations or people and turn this to one's advantage.

Balmy - characterized by pleasantly warm weather.

Tyrannical - exercising power in a cruel or arbitrary way.

Mercurial - subject to sudden or unpredictable changes of mood or mind.

Hence, option d) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the CORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.solution:
Option (b) is the correct answer. "Ostracize" is the correctly spelled word, meaning to exclude or banish someone from a group. The other options contain spelling errors:

(a) "excavatte" should be "excavate," which means to dig or uncover by digging.

(c) "comfortabile" should be "comfortable," indicating a state of ease or physical well-being.

(d) "plagiaraize" should be "plagiarize," which means copying someone else's work or ideas without permission.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Tranquil
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

In the heart of a bustling city, where towering skyscrapers reached for the sky, lived a young orphan named Joseph. With a heart full of determination and a mind filled with curiosity, Joseph embarked on a quest to find his long-lost biological parents. Every day after school, Joseph would sneak into the old library, poring over dusty records and faded photographs. He would spend hours deciphering old birth certificates and piecing together fragments of information, hoping to uncover a clue that would lead him to his past. His friends at the orphanage would often ask why he was so obsessed with his origins. Joseph would smile and say, "I just want to know where I come from. Maybe my parents are out there, looking for me too." As time passed, Liam's determination caught the attention of Ms. Thompson, the librarian. She was intrigued by his dedication and offered to help him in his search. Together, they dug deeper into the archives, their bond growing stronger with every discovery.

One day, buried beneath layers of old papers, they stumbled upon a faded letter. With trembling hands, Joseph unfolded it and read the words that changed his life forever. The letter was from his mother, expressing her love and regret for having to give him up for adoption. She mentioned a special locket that she had left for him as a symbol of their connection. Armed with newfound hope, Joseph set out to find the locket that would lead him to his parents. He followed the clues and embarked on a journey that took him through bustling markets, tranquil parks, and hidden alleyways. Along the way, he encountered kind strangers who offered him guidance and encouragement. Finally, under the shade of an ancient oak tree, Joseph found the locket - a delicate silver heart on a chain. Clutching it tightly, he felt an overwhelming sense of belonging. With a heart full of gratitude, Joseph returned to the orphanage, where he shared his journey with Ms. Thompson and his friends.
questions.solution:
'Tranquil' means free from disturbance; calm. 'Tumultuous' means making a loud, confused noise; uproarious. So, the two words can be used as antonyms of each other. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

Placid- even-tempered.

Serene- calm, peaceful, and untroubled.

Treasured- highly valued; prized.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A speech or piece of writing that praises someone or something highly, especially a tribute to someone who has just died
questions.solution: 'Epitaph' means a phrase or form of words written in memory of a person who has died, especially as an inscription on a tombstone; 'Eulogy' means a speech or piece of writing that praises someone or something highly, especially a tribute to someone who has just died; 'vilification' means abusively disparaging speech or writing; 'denunciation' means a public condemnation of someone or something. According to the meanings mentioned above, b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

It's worth praising the fact that the engineer provided a __________ solution to the complex engineering problem.
questions.solution:
Let's look at the meanings of the given options.

Feasible: able to be made, done, or achieved.

Implausible: difficult to believe, or unlikely.

Unattainable: not able to be achieved.

Sporadic: happening sometimes; not regular or continuous.

"Feasible" is the correct answer as it means possible or practical, which would be appropriate for a solution to a complex engineering problem. The other options do not represent practicality.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: It's worth praising the fact that the engineer provided a feasible solution to the complex engineering problem.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

The team's performance during the championship match was a complete failure or disaster.
questions.solution:
'Fiasco' means a complete failure or disaster. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

'Zealot' means a person who is fanatical and uncompromising in pursuit of their beliefs.

'Nostalgia' means a sentimental longing or affection for the past.

'Serene' means calm, peaceful and untroubled.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the boldened word.

He had to return it as promised, even knowing it was a bogus rule.
questions.solution:
'Bogus' means not genuine or true. 'Sham' means a situation, feeling, system, etc. that is not as good or true as it seems to be.

So, 'valid' is the right antonym.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.question: The word "recreational" most nearly means:
questions.passage:
Directions : In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

River rafting is an exhilarating outdoor activity that combines adventure, teamwork, and a deep engagement with nature. It involves navigating a river's currents using an (5) inflatable raft, often through stretches of turbulent water known as rapids. These rapids are classified on a scale that indicates their difficulty, ranging from gentle flows suitable for beginners to intense, fast-moving sections that demand skill and experience. Participants must work in _(1)_ , following the guide's instructions to paddle in rhythm and maintain balance, as even a slight miscalculation can disrupt the raft's stability. Beyond the thrill, river rafting offers a unique opportunity to _(2)_with the natural environment, as rafters are surrounded by scenic landscapes such as forests, cliffs, and open skies. It also fosters qualities such as trust, communication, and resilience, as each member plays a vital role in navigating the challenges of the river.

However, the activity requires careful attention to safety, and proper gear is _(3)_ to ensure protection against potential risks. In recent years, river rafting has gained popularity as both a (4) recreational pursuit and a form of eco-tourism. When practised responsibly, it encourages appreciation for rivers while promoting sustainable travel practices that help preserve natural ecosystems.
questions.solution: Among the given options, (a) Done for fun and enjoyment is the best fit because "recreational" refers to activities pursued for relaxation, pleasure, or leisure rather than for professional or competitive purposes. Hence, (a) is the correct answer. Done as a serious job relates to professional work, involving high levels of risk emphasises danger, and focused on winning a competition highlights rivalry, none of which convey the sense of leisure inherent in "recreational."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

As the people were generally adaptable, she seldom or ______ had any trouble with them.
questions.solution:
'Seldom' means rarely or almost never. So, 'never' is the right fit to fit in the blank.

Every - used before a singular noun to refer to all the individual members of a set without exception.

Forever - for all future time; for always.

Usually - under normal conditions; generally.

The correct sentence is: As the people were generally adaptable, she seldom or never had any trouble with them.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.question: Select the sentence that has no spelling error.

options.label: A
options.text: His intillectual prowess is commendable and noteworthy.

options.label: B
options.text: The case requires certain level of intellictual capactity.

options.label: C
options.text: School children have different intellectual capabilities.

options.label: D
options.text: Intolectual questions are always appreciated by scholars.

questions.solution:
Among the given sentences, sentence (c) alone has no spelling error.

The word 'intellectual' is wrongly spelt in options a), b), and d), and is correctly spelt in option c).

'Intellectual' means 'involving a person's ability to think and to understand ideas and information'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.question: Choose the sentence with correct collocation for the word 'risk'.

options.label: A
options.text: The company made a big risk by launching the product early.

options.label: B
options.text: The company took a big risk by launching the product early.

options.label: C
options.text: The company created a big risk by launching the product early.

options.label: D
options.text: The company arranged a big risk by launching the product early.

questions.solution: The correct collocation is "take a risk", which means to do something that involves the possibility of failure or danger. "Make a risk", "create a risk", and "arrange a risk" are not standard collocations. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate option.

All pupils are expected to ____ school assembly.
questions.solution:
The correct option to fill in the blank is "attend". 'Attend' means to be present at or participate in an event. In the given context, it indicates that all pupils are expected to be present at a school assembly. Other words do not fit the given context. 'Suspect' means to believe something to be true, typically without evidence. 'Suppose' means to assume something to be the case. 'Pretend' means to act as if something is the case when it is not. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: All pupils are expected to attend school assembly.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.solution:
The incorrectly spelt word is 'Reccomend'.

The correct spelling is "Recommend," which means to suggest something as suitable.

Other words are correctly spelt.

'Proceed' means to go forward.

'Permanent' means lasting indefinitely.

'Participate' means to take part in something.

Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: The word "erosion" as used in the passage most nearly means:
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the passage and answer the questions:

In contemporary discussions on gender equality, the language of feminism has become increasingly common. Many men openly identify themselves as supporters of women's rights and claim to stand in solidarity with feminist ideals. While genuine allies certainly exist, there is also a category of individuals who adopt the label of feminism merely as a social identity rather than a sincere commitment. Their support often appears persuasive on the surface, as they speak the vocabulary of equality and publicly criticise discrimination against women.

However, this performative alignment with feminism can sometimes conceal attitudes that remain deeply patriarchal. A man who openly expresses misogynistic views is usually easier to identify and confront because his position is explicit. In contrast, someone who claims to be progressive while privately perpetuating sexist assumptions may gain trust and social credibility. By presenting themselves as enlightened allies, such individuals often avoid scrutiny and criticism. This contradiction between words and actions allows them to maintain influence in spaces that are meant to promote equality.

The greater danger of such behaviour lies in the erosion of trust it creates. When feminist language is used merely as a tool for personal reputation or social approval, it weakens the authenticity of discussions about gender justice. Women and genuine allies may become sceptical of declarations of support, which ultimately harms collective efforts toward meaningful change. True allyship therefore demands consistency between public claims and private conduct, as well as a willingness to challenge one's own privileges rather than simply adopting the language of progress.

options.label: A
options.text: gradual loss or weakening of confidence or trust

options.label: B
options.text: sudden removal of support or public approval

options.label: C
options.text: deliberate rejection of ideas or social movements

options.label: D
options.text: strong criticism expressed in public discussions

questions.solution: The word appears in Paragraph 3 in the phrase "the erosion of trust." In this context, the passage explains that when feminist language is used merely for reputation or social approval, it gradually weakens the authenticity of discussions about gender justice. Thus, "erosion" refers to a slow or gradual loss rather than a sudden event. Therefore, "gradual loss or weakening of confidence or trust" best matches the contextual meaning. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Cogent
questions.solution: 'Cogent' means '(Adj)(of an argument or case) clear, logical, and convincing'. Options a) and b) can be rejected as they are unrelated to the word. 'Vague' means 'Of uncertain, indefinite, or unclear character or meaning'. Hence, option c) can also be rejected as it is the exact opposite. 'Erudite' means 'Having or showing great knowledge or learning'. 'Quixotic' means 'Extremely idealistic; unrealistic and impractical'. Hence, option d) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word:

The tailor will first baste the dress together with loose stitches for a fitting.

options.label: A
options.text: She remembered to baste the turkey every 30 minutes to keep it moist.

options.label: B
options.text: The instructions say to baste the sleeves onto the bodice before sewing.

options.label: C
options.text: He used a contrasting thread to baste the hem so he could see it easily.

options.label: D
options.text: To prepare for sewing, baste the pattern pieces together.

questions.solution:
A homonym is a word that is spelled and pronounced the same as another word but has a different meaning.

In the original sentence, "baste" is a sewing term that means to tack or sew with long, loose, temporary stitches.

In options (b), (c), and (d), "baste" is used with the exact same sewing meaning.

In option (a), "baste" is a cooking term that means to pour juices or melted fat over food (especially meat) during cooking to keep it moist. This is a completely different meaning, making it the correct homonym.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: The word "intrusive" in the passage most nearly means:
questions.passage:
Directions :Read the passage and answer the questions:

In professional environments, the hiring process is expected to be guided by fairness, objectivity, and relevance to the role. However, a persistent concern that continues to undermine these principles is the tendency of some human resource professionals to ask female candidates intrusive personal questions during interviews. Queries about marital status, plans for motherhood, childcare responsibilities, or living arrangements are frequently directed at women, while male candidates are rarely subjected to similar scrutiny. This disparity reflects deep-rooted gender bias and raises serious ethical concerns about the integrity of recruitment practices. Such questioning shifts the focus away from merit and towards personal circumstances that have little to no connection with professional capability.

These questions are fundamentally irrelevant to assessing a candidate's competence, dedication, or potential contribution to an organisation. By probing into personal life choices, interviewers often operate on the assumption that women may be less committed or less flexible due to familial responsibilities. This not only disadvantages qualified candidates but also reinforces outdated stereotypes that continue to hinder workplace equality. Moreover, it creates an uncomfortable and discriminatory environment where women are compelled to justify aspects of their lives that should remain private. As a result, the principle of equal opportunity is compromised, and the hiring process becomes biased rather than merit-driven.

Ethical hiring practices must prioritise neutrality, relevance, and respect. Employers can legitimately outline job requirements such as relocation, travel, or working hours, but these should be framed in a manner that applies equally to all candidates, regardless of gender. Instead of asking personal questions, interviewers should focus on whether candidates are able to meet the professional demands of the role. Addressing this issue requires awareness and accountability, with organisations taking active steps to train hiring personnel and eliminate biased questioning patterns. Creating a fair and inclusive interview process is essential for building a progressive workplace where individuals are evaluated solely on their skills and qualifications.

options.label: A
options.text: Respectful of personal boundaries and privacy.

options.label: B
options.text: Involving unnecessary interference into private matters.

options.label: C
options.text: Focused only on professional qualifications and skills.

options.label: D
options.text: Intended to simplify the hiring process efficiently.

questions.solution: In the context of the passage, "intrusive" refers to personal questions that invade a candidate's private life without relevance to the job. Therefore, it implies unnecessary interference into private matters. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in a sentence.

As the city woke up, the cacophony of honking horns, shouting vendors, and bustling crowds filled the air.
questions.solution:
Cacophony: A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds.

Discord: Lack of harmony or agreement.

Harmony: The quality of forming a consistent and orderly whole to produce a pleasing and balanced sound.

Noise: A sound, especially one that is loud, unpleasant, or causes disturbance.

Dissonance: A harsh and unpleasant combination of sounds.

Among the given options, the word 'harmony' is opposite in meaning to the word 'cacophony'. So, the two words can be used as antonyms of each other.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank.

He stacked books neatly to form a _____ on the desk.
questions.solution:
The given sentence describes how the person neatly stacked books on the desk. Among the given options, 'pile' fits the blank appropriately as it refers to a collection of things laid or stacked on top of each other. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The final sentence: He stacked books neatly to form a pile on the desk.

"Peel" refers to removing the outer covering or skin of something.

"Peal" refers to a loud ringing of bells or a loud sound of laughter or thunder.

"Peer" refers to someone who is of equal standing or status.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The security guard remained prepared and alert, diligently patrolling the premises.
questions.solution:
On the ball: This idiom is used to describe someone who is alert, competent, and fully aware of what is going on. In the context of the sentence, if we replace "prepared and alert" with "On the ball," the sentence would read, "The security guard remained on the ball, diligently patrolling the premises." This conveys the idea that the security guard is not only prepared but also actively aware and competent in carrying out their duties. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

On the fence: This idiom means to be undecided or neutral about a situation.

Air rage: This term refers to disruptive or violent behaviour on an aircraft.

Off one's rocker: This idiom means to be crazy or mentally unstable.

questions.question:
Select the sentence that uses the given idiom correctly.

Break a leg

options.label: A
options.text: Herman broke a leg when he slipped on the ice.

options.label: B
options.text: Sheela told her friend to break a leg before his big performance.

options.label: C
options.text: I broke a leg while I was running a marathon.

options.label: D
options.text: The dog broke a leg when he fell off the cliff.

questions.solution:
The idiom "break a leg" is used to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance or an important event. Among the given options, option (b) correctly uses the idiom to describe someone encouraging another person to perform well before a big performance. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The rest of the options use the idiom incorrectly.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate collocation to substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

He added that all candidates should give the exam on the same day to avoid 'potential unfairness'.
questions.solution:
Collocation is the combination of words formed when two or more words are often used together in a way that sounds correct.

The correct collocation is "take the exam" which means "to have one's knowledge or ability tested formally, often in writing".

Other options are incorrect collocations.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Contain
questions.solution:
Contain: to have as a part, or be equal to; include.

Include: comprise or contain as part of a whole.

So, both words are similar in meaning. Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Give: freely transfer the possession of (something) to (someone).

Appear: come into sight; become visible or noticeable, especially without apparent cause.

Reject: dismiss as inadequate, unacceptable, or faulty.
